docs.text:
Section under development

This section is currently being built. Content will be added progressively. Check back soon!

This section provides practical guides and quick-start resources for umfoam — an OpenFOAM-based solver for urban microclimate simulations. The goal is to lower the barrier to entry for researchers and practitioners who want to run urban CFD simulations.

docs.title: 🔧 umfoam Installation
docs.text: Step-by-step installation guide for umfoam on Linux systems. Covers dependencies, compilation from source, and environment setup.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick-Start Cases
docs.text: Ready-to-run tutorial cases with annotated setup files. Designed to get you from zero to a working simulation in under an hour.

docs.title: 🌬️ Boundary Conditions Reference
docs.text: Reference guide for the boundary conditions used in urban microclimate simulations: inlet profiles, wall functions, atmospheric boundary layer setup, and tree canopy conditions.

docs.title: 🧊 Meshing Helpers
docs.text: Tips and scripts for generating urban meshes using cfMesh and snappyHexMesh. Includes guidance on geometry preparation, refinement levels, and quality checks.

docs.title: 📊 Post-Processing Tips
docs.text:
Workflows for extracting and visualising results: mean flow fields, turbulence statistics, thermal comfort indices (PET, UTCI), and time-series analysis.

More sections to come. Contact me if you have specific topics you'd like covered.

docs.title: Research
docs.text: My research sits at the intersection of urban physics, computational fluid dynamics, and environmental sustainability. I develop and apply high-fidelity CFD models to investigate the physical processes that govern urban microclimates, with the aim of supporting evidence-based urban design.

docs.title: Research Interests
docs.text:
Urban Microclimate & Thermal Comfort Understanding how urban morphology — building layouts, street geometry, vegetation — governs local temperature, wind speed, and human thermal comfort. I combine CFD simulations with thermal comfort indices to evaluate outdoor spaces under realistic meteorological conditions.

Wind Flow in Urban Environments Modelling wind flow around buildings, including the complex aerodynamics of lift-up structures and street canyons. I use porous media approaches and high-resolution CFD to capture flow features relevant to ventilation and pollutant dispersion.

Urban Vegetation & Cooling Quantifying the cooling potential of trees and green infrastructure in city neighbourhoods. My work addresses both the direct shading effect and the indirect evapotranspiration cooling, across different climate contexts including temperate and tropical hot-humid cities.

Data-Driven Urban Climate Analysis Applying clustering and machine learning techniques to CFD-derived time-series data to identify and characterize urban microclimate zones — enabling scalable analysis of large, heterogeneous urban domains.
